<instructions>
Build a timezone overlap checker web app using a popular web framework of your choice. Do NOT use vanilla JS or a raw Node.js `http` server. The app must run with a single command (`npm run dev` or equivalent).

You have **full creative freedom** on everything: technology choices, code architecture, file structure, component separation, state management, styling approach, design system, and UX. Own every decision — make it clean, well-structured, and something you're proud of.
</instructions>

<purpose>
A tool for remote workers, distributed teams, and digital nomads who need to find common meeting windows or compare their schedule against colleagues in other timezones.
</purpose>

<modes>
The app has two modes the user can toggle between:

**Meeting Mode** (default)
Find hours when everyone across all selected cities is simultaneously awake. All cities share the same highlighted overlap window. Think: scheduling a group call where every participant must be available.

**Base Mode**
One city is the "base" (the reference). Each other city gets its own independent overlap calculated only against the base. Different cities may highlight different hours. Think: a person living in one city who works with people in several other cities and wants to see per-person availability.
</modes>

<cities>
- Users maintain a list of cities to compare. Default: San Francisco, Denpasar, Geneva.
- Cities come from a predefined catalog of ~34 cities spanning all major world regions (North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Middle East, Asia, Oceania).
- Users add cities via a searchable dropdown (search by city name or country). Remove any city from the list. No duplicates allowed.
- No custom/arbitrary timezone entries — only the predefined catalog.
</cities>

<reference-city>
- The first city in the list is always the **reference city**, visually marked (e.g. a "REF" badge).
- All hour calculations are anchored to the reference city's timezone.
- Users can click any city's name to promote it as the new reference (it moves to the top).
- In Base Mode, overlap is computed between the reference city and each other city independently.
</reference-city>

<availability>
Users configure their personal "awake window" via a settings panel:

- **Wake-up hour** (0–23, default: 7)
- **Sleep hour** (0–23, default: 23)
- **Time format**: 12h or 24h (default: 12h)

The awake window applies uniformly to all cities (everyone shares the same sleep schedule). Overnight ranges are supported (e.g. wake at 22, sleep at 6 for night-shift workers). Changes take effect immediately.
</availability>

<grid>
The core visualization is a **24-column grid** (one column per hour of the reference city's day, 0–23).

Each cell shows what hour it is **locally** in that city when it's that column's hour in the reference city.

Three visual states per cell:
1. **Sleeping** — the local hour falls outside the awake window → faded/muted
2. **Awake, no overlap** — awake but not part of the overlap → neutral
3. **Overlap** — awake AND this hour qualifies as overlap → highlighted (e.g. green), bold text
</grid>

<overlap-summary>
Displayed above the grid when 2+ cities are present:

- **Meeting Mode**: total overlap hours count + time range(s) in the reference city's timezone. Zero overlap → warning message.
- **Base Mode**: one line per non-reference city, each with its own overlap count + time range(s). Zero overlap → individual warning.

Time ranges are inclusive start → exclusive end (e.g. "9am — 12pm" = hours 9, 10, 11). Non-contiguous windows are shown as separate badges/ranges.
</overlap-summary>

<timezone-math>
- UTC offsets derived from the current date → DST is automatically handled.
- Fractional offsets supported (e.g. India UTC+5:30, Nepal UTC+5:45).
- Each city displays its current UTC offset.
</timezone-math>

<responsive>
**Desktop (≥768px)**: cities as rows, hours as columns (horizontal grid). Left: city info + REF badge + UTC offset. Center: 24 hour cells. Right: remove button.

**Mobile (<768px)**: cities as columns, hours as rows (vertical layout). These are **two separate layouts**, not a single responsive grid.
</responsive>

<persistence>
All state (city list, settings, active mode) is persisted to localStorage. Refreshing restores the last configuration. A new browser/incognito session starts with defaults.
</persistence>

<defaults>
On first visit:
- 3 cities: San Francisco, Denpasar, Geneva
- Meeting mode active
- Awake window: 7am–11pm
- 12-hour format
- Overlap summary showing common availability across the 3 default cities
- A hint at the bottom: "Green cells = everyone awake"
</defaults>

<important>
- `<title>` and page heading must be your model name (e.g. "Claude Sonnet 4.5" or "GPT-4o")
- The grid must make overlaps **instantly obvious** — alignment is critical
- Full creative freedom on colors, typography, and visual style — design the best possible UI/UX
- Polished, production-quality — not a prototype
</important>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9321, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

text: Since

the directory is empty, I'm scaffolding a Vite + React + TypeScript app with Tailwind from scratch, writing files directly instead of using the wizard. I'll keep dependencies minimal, favoring a simple reducer with a
localStorage hook over adding something like zustand.
Actually, z
ustand with
persist middleware is cleaner, so I'll go with that. I'm planning out the file structure: config files, main app entry, a data file with 34 cities,
timezone and overlap calculation libraries, a zustand store, and a set of components for header, mode toggle, settings, city picker, overlap summary, and grid/cell displays for both

desktop and mobile, plus possibly vitest for testing the math utilities.

For timezone math, I'm using Intl.DateTimeFormat to compute UTC offset min

utes for a given timezone and date by formatting parts and diffing against a constructed UTC timestamp, then deriving each city's local hour relative to a reference hour with wraparound and formatting
it as a readable time string.
Now I'm working out
the aw
ake/
as
leep logic:
com
paring local
minutes against a wake/sleep window, handling the normal case, the overnight-wrap case where sleep is earlier than wake, and the edge case where wake equals sleep me
aning always awake, all at minute-level precision to handle fractional UTC offsets correctly. For overlap logic, I'm deciding that in meeting mode all c
ities need to be awake at a given hour, while in base mode each city is compared against the reference city's awake status, and I'm figuring out how the reference row itself should highlight—le
aning toward showing hours where the reference is awake and at least one other city overlaps.
I
'm also planning how to merge contiguous awake hours into readable ranges, including handling wraparound across midnight so a run like 10pm to 2am displays as one range inst
ead of splitting at the day boundary. For visual design I'm settling on a dark slate theme with emerald highlights for overlapping hours and using the
system font stack to avoid network fetches while keeping it polished. For mobile I'm planning a layout with hours as rows and sticky city name columns, toggling vis
ibility between mobile and desktop breakpoints, and starting to build out the city catalog data.
I
'm now trimming the full city list down to about 34 representative timezones, cutting each region's count roughly in half while keeping major h
ubs like San Francisco, New York, London, Lisbon, Cairo, and Istanbul.
Now
I'm planning the actual implementation—thinking through package.json dependencies (React, Zustand for persisted settings stor
age) before starting the build.

+export const MINUTES_PER_DAY = 24 * 60
+
+const formatterCache = new Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>()
+
+function getFormatter(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
+  let formatter = formatterCache.get(timeZone)
+  if (!formatter) {
+    formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
+      timeZone,
+      hourCycle: 'h23',
+      year: 'numeric',
+      month: 'numeric',
+      day: 'numeric',
+      hour: 'numeric',
+      minute: 'numeric',
+      second: 'numeric',
+    })
+    formatterCache.set(timeZone, formatter)
+  }
+  return formatter
+}
+
+/**
+ * UTC offset of `timeZone` at the given instant, in minutes (east-positive).
+ * Derived from Intl so DST is handled by the runtime's tz database.
+ */
+export function getUtcOffsetMinutes(timeZone: string, at: Date = new Date()): number {
+  const parts = getFormatter(timeZone).formatToParts(at)
+  const read = (type: Intl.DateTimeFormatPartTypes) =>
+    Number(parts.find((part) => part.type === type)?.value ?? 0)
+
+  const asUtc = Date.UTC(
+    read('year'),
+    read('month') - 1,
+    read('day'),
+    read('hour') % 24,
+    read('minute'),
+    read('second'),
+  )
+  // Drop sub-second drift so the offset is an exact number of minutes.
+  const instant = Math.floor(at.getTime() / 1000) * 1000
+  return Math.round((asUtc - instant) / 60_000)
+}
+
+/** e.g. "UTC+5:30", "UTC-7", "UTC±0" */
+export function formatUtcOffset(offsetMinutes: number): string {
+  if (offsetMinutes === 0) return 'UTC±0'
+  const sign = offsetMinutes > 0 ? '+' : '-'
+  const abs = Math.abs(offsetMinutes)
+  const hours = Math.floor(abs / 60)
+  const minutes = abs % 60
+  return `UTC${sign}${hours}${minutes ? `:${String(minutes).padStart(2, '0')}` : ''}`
+}
+
+/** Wrap a minute-of-day value into [0, 1440). */
+export function wrapMinutes(minutes: number): number {
+  return ((minutes % MINUTES_PER_DAY) + MINUTES_PER_DAY) % MINUTES_PER_DAY
+}
+
+/**
+ * Local minute-of-day in a city when it is `referenceHour` o'clock in the
+ * reference city.
+ */
+export function localMinuteOfDay(
+  referenceHour: number,
+  referenceOffset: number,
+  cityOffset: number,
+): number {
+  return wrapMinutes(referenceHour * 60 + (cityOffset - referenceOffset))
+}
+
+export type TimeFormat = '12h' | '24h'
+
+interface FormatHourOptions {
+  /** Include ":mm" even when minutes are zero. */
+  padded?: boolean
+}
+
+/** Format a minute-of-day value, e.g. 570 → "9:30am" / "09:30". */
+export function formatMinuteOfDay(
+  minuteOfDay: number,
+  format: TimeFormat,
+  { padded = false }: FormatHourOptions = {},
+): string {
+  const wrapped = wrapMinutes(minuteOfDay)
+  const hours = Math.floor(wrapped / 60)
+  const minutes = wrapped % 60
+  const mm = String(minutes).padStart(2, '0')
+
+  if (format === '24h') {
+    return `${String(hours).padStart(2, '0')}:${mm}`
+  }
+
+  const suffix = hours < 12 ? 'am' : 'pm'
+  const hour12 = hours % 12 === 0 ? 12 : hours % 12
+  const showMinutes = padded || minutes !== 0
+  return `${hour12}${showMinutes ? `:${mm}` : ''}${suffix}`
+}
+
+/** Short label for a whole hour used in select options and axis headers. */
+export function formatHour(hour: number, format: TimeFormat): string {
+  return formatMinuteOfDay(hour * 60, format)
+}

+import type { City } from '@/data/cities'
+import { getUtcOffsetMinutes, localMinuteOfDay } from './timezone'
+
+export type Mode = 'meeting' | 'base'
+
+export interface AwakeWindow {
+  /** Hour (0–23) the awake window starts, inclusive. */
+  wakeHour: number
+  /** Hour (0–23) the awake window ends, exclusive. */
+  sleepHour: number
+}
+
+export type CellState = 'sleeping' | 'awake' | 'overlap'
+
+export interface HourCell {
+  /** Hour of the reference city's day (0–23) this cell belongs to. */
+  referenceHour: number
+  /** Local minute-of-day in this city at that reference hour. */
+  localMinute: number
+  state: CellState
+}
+
+export interface CityRow {
+  city: City
+  offsetMinutes: number
+  isReference: boolean
+  cells: HourCell[]
+}
+
+export interface HourRange {
+  /** Inclusive start hour in reference time. */
+  start: number
+  /** Exclusive end hour in reference time; may exceed 23 when wrapping midnight. */
+  end: number
+}
+
+export interface OverlapResult {
+  hours: number[]
+  ranges: HourRange[]
+}
+
+export interface Schedule {
+  rows: CityRow[]
+  /** Meeting mode: overlap shared by every city. */
+  meeting: OverlapResult
+  /** Base mode: overlap of each non-reference city with the reference, keyed by city id. */
+  perCity: Map<string, OverlapResult>
+}
+
+export const HOURS = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, hour) => hour)
+
+/**
+ * Whether a local minute-of-day falls inside the awake window.
+ * Supports overnight windows (wake 22 → sleep 6). Equal hours = always awake.
+ */
+export function isAwake(localMinute: number, { wakeHour, sleepHour }: AwakeWindow): boolean {
+  const wake = wakeHour * 60
+  const sleep = sleepHour * 60
+  if (wake === sleep) return true
+  if (wake < sleep) return localMinute >= wake && localMinute < sleep
+  return localMinute >= wake || localMinute < sleep
+}
+
+/** Collapse a sorted list of hours into contiguous [start, end) ranges, merging across midnight. */
+export function hoursToRanges(hours: number[]): HourRange[] {
+  if (hours.length === 0) return []
+  const sorted = [...new Set(hours)].sort((a, b) => a - b)
+  if (sorted.length === 24) return [{ start: 0, end: 24 }]
+
+  const ranges: HourRange[] = []
+  let start = sorted[0]
+  let previous = sorted[0]
+  for (const hour of sorted.slice(1)) {
+    if (hour === previous + 1) {
+      previous = hour
+      continue
+    }
+    ranges.push({ start, end: previous + 1 })
+    start = hour
+    previous = hour
+  }
+  ranges.push({ start, end: previous + 1 })
+
+  // A range ending at midnight followed by one starting at 0 is one window that wraps.
+  if (ranges.length > 1) {
+    const first = ranges[0]
+    const last = ranges[ranges.length - 1]
+    if (first.start === 0 && last.end === 24) {
+      ranges.pop()
+      ranges.shift()
+      ranges.push({ start: last.start, end: 24 + first.end })
+    }
+  }
+  return ranges
+}
+
+function toResult(hours: number[]): OverlapResult {
+  return { hours, ranges: hoursToRanges(hours) }
+}
+
+export function computeSchedule(
+  cities: City[],
+  window: AwakeWindow,
+  mode: Mode,
+  now: Date = new Date(),
+): Schedule {
+  if (cities.length === 0) {
+    return { rows: [], meeting: toResult([]), perCity: new Map() }
+  }
+
+  const offsets = cities.map((city) => getUtcOffsetMinutes(city.timeZone, now))
+  const referenceOffset = offsets[0]
+
+  const awakeMatrix = cities.map((_, index) =>
+    HOURS.map((hour) => isAwake(localMinuteOfDay(hour, referenceOffset, offsets[index]), window)),
+  )
+  const referenceAwake = awakeMatrix[0]
+
+  const meetingHours = HOURS.filter((hour) => awakeMatrix.every((row) => row[hour]))
+
+  const perCity = new Map<string, OverlapResult>()
+  for (let index = 1; index < cities.length; index++) {
+    const hours = HOURS.filter((hour) => referenceAwake[hour] && awakeMatrix[index][hour])
+    perCity.set(cities[index].id, toResult(hours))
+  }
+
+  // In base mode the reference row lights up wherever at least one colleague is reachable.
+  const referenceBaseHours = new Set<number>()
+  for (const result of perCity.values()) result.hours.forEach((hour) => referenceBaseHours.add(hour))
+
+  const rows: CityRow[] = cities.map((city, index) => {
+    const isReference = index === 0
+    const highlighted: ReadonlySet<number> =
+      mode === 'meeting'
+        ? new Set(meetingHours)
+        : isReference
+          ? referenceBaseHours
+          : new Set(perCity.get(city.id)?.hours ?? [])
+
+    const cells: HourCell[] = HOURS.map((hour) => {
+      const awake = awakeMatrix[index][hour]
+      const state: CellState = !awake ? 'sleeping' : highlighted.has(hour) ? 'overlap' : 'awake'
+      return {
+        referenceHour: hour,
+        localMinute: localMinuteOfDay(hour, referenceOffset, offsets[index]),
+        state,
+      }
+    })
+
+    return { city, offsetMinutes: offsets[index], isReference, cells }
+  })
+
+  return { rows, meeting: toResult(meetingHours), perCity }
+}

+  sleepHour: 23,
+  timeFormat: '12h',
+}
+

+
+const clampHour = (value: number, fallback: number) =>

+import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react'
+import { getCity, type City } from '@/data/cities'
+import { computeSchedule, type Schedule } from '@/lib/overlap'
+import { useAppStore } from '@/store/useAppStore'
+
+const REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000
+
+/** Ticks once a minute so offsets stay correct across DST transitions in a long-lived tab. */
+function useNow(): Date {
+  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => new Date())
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const id = window.setInterval(() => setNow(new Date()), REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS)
+    return () => window.clearInterval(id)
+  }, [])
+  return now
+}
+
+export function useSelectedCities(): City[] {
+  const cityIds = useAppStore((state) => state.cityIds)
+  return useMemo(
+    () => cityIds.map((id) => getCity(id)).filter((city): city is City => city !== undefined),
+    [cityIds],
+  )
+}
+
+export function useSchedule(): Schedule {
+  const cities = useSelectedCities()
+  const mode = useAppStore((state) => state.mode)
+  const wakeHour = useAppStore((state) => state.settings.wakeHour)
+  const sleepHour = useAppStore((state) => state.settings.sleepHour)
+  const now = useNow()
+
+  return useMemo(
+    () => computeSchedule(cities, { wakeHour, sleepHour }, mode, now),
+    [cities, wakeHour, sleepHour, mode, now],
+  )
+}

  Node/Playwright/Chromium dependencies to perform the same page-load,
  screenshot, console-error, and interaction checks without installing
  anything.
- Only install the CLI when npm is allowed for the current workspace and the
  task really needs `dev-browser` persistence or CDP attachment that the
  bundled browser runtime cannot provide.

```bash
npm install -g dev-browser
dev-browser install
```

When falling back to Playwright, preserve the same proof standard: record the
URL, title, console/page errors, screenshots or output artifacts, and the exact
interaction steps that were executed. State clearly that the `dev-browser` CLI
was unavailable and that the fallback used real browser automation.

## Core Pattern

Write small, focused scripts. Each script does ONE thing. End by logging state for next decision.

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.goto("https://example.com");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ url: page.url(), title: await page.title() }, null, 2));
EOF
```

## CLI Flags

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--headless` | Launch Chromium in headless mode |
| `--connect [URL]` | Connect to running Chrome/Chromium via CDP (auto-discover Chrome, or use a specific CDP endpoint) |
| `--browser <NAME>` | Select named browser instance (default: "default") |
| `--timeout <SECONDS>` | Max script execution time (default: 30) |

## Browser API

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `browser.getPage(name)` | Get/create named page (persists between scripts) |
| `browser.newPage()` | Create anonymous page (auto-cleanup after script) |
| `browser.listPages()` | List all tabs: `[{id, url, title, name}]` |
| `browser.closePage(name)` | Close named page |

## File I/O (restricted to `~/.dev-browser/tmp/`)

Never pass absolute paths to `saveScreenshot` or `writeFile`. If a task asks for screenshots or reports in a scratchpad/output directory, save with a relative name first, then copy the returned `~/.dev-browser/tmp/...` file to the requested path from the shell.

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `await saveScreenshot(buf, name)` | Save screenshot buffer, returns path |
| `await writeFile(name, data)` | Write file, returns path |
| `await readFile(name)` | Read file, returns content |

## Key Workflows

### Discover Unknown Page

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.goto("https://example.com");
const result = await page.snapshotForAI();
console.log(result.full);
EOF
```

Then interact based on discovered elements:
```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }).click();
const result = await page.snapshotForAI({ track: "main" });
console.log(result.full);
EOF
```

### Take Screenshot

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
const buf = await page.screenshot();
const path = await saveScreenshot(buf, "debug.png");
console.log(path);
EOF
```

### Fill Form

```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
await page.fill("#email", "user@example.com");
await page.fill("#password", "secret");
await page.click("button[type=submit]");
await page.waitForURL("**/dashboard");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ url: page.url(), title: await page.title() }, null, 2));
EOF
```

### Connect to Running Chrome

```bash
dev-browser --connect <<'EOF'
const tabs = await browser.listPages();
console.log(JSON.stringify(tabs, null, 2));
EOF
```

### Connect to Helium via CDP

Helium is Chromium-based and can be controlled by `dev-browser` when launched with remote debugging enabled. `dev-browser --connect` auto-discovery does not find Helium, so always pass the explicit CDP endpoint.

For a separate automation profile:
```bash
"/Applications/Helium.app/Contents/MacOS/Helium" \
  --remote-debugging-port=9334 \
  --user-data-dir=/tmp/helium-dev-browser-profile \
  --no-first-run \
  --no-default-browser-check
```

Then connect:
```bash
dev-browser --browser helium --connect http://127.0.0.1:9334 <<'EOF'
const tabs = await browser.listPages();
console.log(JSON.stringify(tabs, null, 2));
EOF
```

To automate the user's existing Helium session, Helium must be fully quit and relaunched with `--remote-debugging-port`; an already-running Helium instance that was started without remote debugging cannot be attached by `dev-browser`.

```bash
"/Applications/Helium.app/Contents/MacOS/Helium" --remote-debugging-port=9334
dev-browser --browser helium --connect http://127.0.0.1:9334
```

If Helium is already open without CDP and must not be restarted, use AppleScript or Computer Use for UI-level control instead of `dev-browser`.

### Error Recovery

If a script fails, the page stays where it stopped. Reconnect and inspect:
```bash
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
const path = await saveScreenshot(await page.screenshot(), "debug.png");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ screenshot: path, url: page.url(), title: await page.title() }, null, 2));
EOF
```

## Tips

- Use `page.snapshotForAI()` for structure discovery; use screenshots for visual layout
- Keep page names stable across scripts to resume after failures
- Use `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))` for structured output
- Use `--timeout 10` for scripts that should fail fast
- Pages from `browser.getPage("name")` persist between script runs - no need to re-navigate
- Inside `page.evaluate(...)`, use plain JavaScript only - no TypeScript

## Full API Reference

For complete Playwright Page methods and advanced patterns, see [references/api-reference.md](references/api-reference.md).

# Timezone overlap checker

Find the hours when a distributed team is awake at the same time. Pick cities from a
curated catalog of 34, set your awake window, and read the overlap straight off a
24-hour grid anchored to a reference city.

## Run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:9321
```

Other scripts: `pnpm build`, `pnpm preview`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`.

## Stack

- React 19 + TypeScript, bundled by Vite
- Tailwind CSS v4 for styling
- Zustand (with `persist`) for state, saved to `localStorage`
- Vitest for the timezone and overlap math

## How it works

- **Reference city** — the first city in the list. Every column is one hour of its day.
  Click any other city's name to promote it.
- **Meeting mode** — highlights hours when *every* city is inside the awake window.
- **Base mode** — highlights, per city, the hours it shares with the reference only.
  The reference row lights up wherever at least one colleague is reachable.
- **Awake window** — wake/sleep hours apply to all cities and may wrap overnight.
- **Offsets** — computed from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for the current instant, so DST
  and fractional zones (India, Nepal) fall out for free. A minute-level tick keeps a
  long-lived tab accurate.

## Layout

```
src/
  data/cities.ts        catalog + search
  lib/timezone.ts       offsets, local-time math, formatting
  lib/overlap.ts        awake windows, overlap, ranges, grid model
  store/useAppStore.ts  persisted state
  hooks/useSchedule.ts  derives the grid model from state
  components/           header, mode toggle, settings, city picker,
                        overlap summary, desktop + mobile grids
```

Desktop (≥768px) renders cities as rows; mobile renders cities as columns. They are
two separate components rather than one reflowing grid.

# Timezone overlap checker

Find the hours when a distributed team is awake at the same time. Pick cities from a
curated catalog of 34, set your awake window, and read the overlap straight off a
24-hour grid anchored to a reference city.

## Run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:9321
```

Other scripts: `pnpm build`, `pnpm preview`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`.

## Stack

- React 19 + TypeScript, bundled by Vite
- Tailwind CSS v4 for styling
- Zustand (with `persist`) for state, saved to `localStorage`
- Vitest for the timezone and overlap math

## How it works

- **Reference city** — the first city in the list. Every column is one hour of its day.
  Click any other city's name to promote it.
- **Meeting mode** — highlights hours when *every* city is inside the awake window.
- **Base mode** — highlights, per city, the hours it shares with the reference only.
  The reference row lights up wherever at least one colleague is reachable.
- **Awake window** — wake/sleep hours apply to all cities and may wrap overnight.
- **Offsets** — computed from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for the current instant, so DST
  and fractional zones (India, Nepal) fall out for free. A minute-level tick keeps a
  long-lived tab accurate.

## Layout

```
src/
  data/cities.ts        catalog + search
  lib/timezone.ts       offsets, local-time math, formatting
  lib/overlap.ts        awake windows, overlap, ranges, grid model
  store/useAppStore.ts  persisted state
  hooks/useSchedule.ts  derives the grid model from state
  components/           header, mode toggle, settings, city picker,
                        overlap summary, desktop + mobile grids
```

Desktop (≥768px) renders cities as rows; mobile renders cities as columns. They are
two separate components rather than one reflowing grid.
